title: Cardiac Arrest
overview: Unresponsive person who is not breathing normally. Begin CPR immediately.

steps.title: Check responsiveness
steps.description: Shake the person's shoulders and shout. If no response, call 112 immediately.

steps.title: Lay them flat
steps.description: Place the person on their back on a firm, flat surface.

steps.title: Open the airway
steps.description: Tilt the head back gently and lift the chin to open the airway. Check for breathing for no more than 10 seconds.

steps.title: Chest compressions
steps.description: Place the heel of your hand on the centre of the chest. Push down hard and fast — at least 5 cm deep, 100-120 times per minute. Do 30 compressions.

steps.title: Rescue breaths
steps.description: Pinch the nose, seal your mouth over theirs, and give 2 slow rescue breaths. Watch the chest rise. Continue 30 compressions then 2 breaths until help arrives.

title: Choking (Adult)
overview: Adult who cannot breathe, speak, or cough effectively due to a blocked airway.

steps.title: Confirm choking
steps.description: Ask 'Are you choking?' If they cannot speak, cough, or breathe, act immediately. If they can cough, encourage them to keep coughing.

steps.title: Lean them forward
steps.description: Stand behind them. Ask them to lean forward with their head lower than their chest.

steps.title: 5 back blows
steps.description: Using the heel of your hand, give 5 firm blows between the shoulder blades. Check after each blow if the blockage has cleared.

steps.title: 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich)
steps.description: If back blows fail, stand behind them and wrap your arms around their waist. Make a fist and place it just above the navel. Grasp with your other hand and thrust sharply inward and upward. Repeat up to 5 times. Alternate with back blows until the object is dislodged or the person loses consciousness.

title: Severe Bleeding
overview: Serious wound with heavy blood loss that will not stop on its own.

steps.title: Apply direct pressure
steps.description: Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth, bandage, or clothing. Do not remove the cloth — if it soaks through, add more on top.

steps.title: Elevate if possible
steps.description: If the wound is on an arm or leg and no bones are broken, raise the limb above the level of the heart.

steps.title: Maintain pressure
steps.description: Keep firm continuous pressure on the wound. Do not peek — lifting the cloth disrupts clotting. Maintain for at least 10–15 minutes.

steps.title: Call 112 and monitor
steps.description: Keep the person still and calm. Watch for signs of shock: pale skin, rapid weak pulse, confusion. Lay them down and keep them warm.

title: Burns
overview: Skin damage from heat, chemicals, or electricity.

steps.title: Remove from source
steps.description: Get the person away from the heat source. Do not touch them if they are in contact with electricity — turn off the power first.

steps.title: Cool with water
steps.description: Run cool (not cold) clean water over the burn for 20 minutes. Do not stop early — 20 minutes is essential to stop the burning process.

steps.title: Do NOT use ice or home remedies
steps.description: Never apply ice, butter, toothpaste, oil, or any other substance. These make burns worse and increase infection risk.

steps.title: Remove jewellery
steps.description: Carefully remove watches, rings, and tight clothing near the burn area before swelling begins. Do not pull off anything stuck to the skin.

steps.title: Cover loosely
steps.description: Cover the burn loosely with a clean non-fluffy material such as cling film or a clean plastic bag. Seek medical help for burns larger than the person's hand.

title: Fracture (Broken Bone)
overview: Suspected broken bone — do not move the injured area.

steps.title: Do not straighten
steps.description: Never try to straighten a broken bone. Immobilise it in the position you find it.

steps.title: Support the injury
steps.description: Support the limb above and below the injury using cushions, folded clothing, or your hands. Keep the person still.

steps.title: Apply a splint if available
steps.description: You can use a rolled newspaper, stick, or firm object padded with cloth as a splint. Tie it in place — not too tight. Check circulation by pressing a fingernail or toenail until white, then release; colour should return in 2 seconds.

steps.title: Do not give food or water
steps.description: The person may need surgery. Do not give food, water, or pain medication without medical advice. Call 112 and keep them warm and still.

title: Drowning
overview: Person removed from water who is unresponsive or not breathing normally.

steps.title: Remove from water safely
steps.description: Only enter water to rescue if you are a trained rescuer. Otherwise use a rope, branch, clothing, or lifebuoy to pull them to safety. Protect your own life.

steps.title: Call 112
steps.description: Call for help immediately. Note the exact location.

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.description: Lay the person on their back. Tilt the head back and check for breathing for up to 10 seconds. Do not waste time trying to remove water from the lungs.

steps.title: Give rescue breaths first
steps.description: Unlike regular CPR, give 5 initial rescue breaths before starting chest compressions. Pinch the nose, seal your mouth over theirs, and breathe steadily for 1 second each.

steps.title: CPR 30:2
steps.description: Begin CPR — 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. Continue until the person starts breathing, help arrives, or you are too exhausted to continue.

title: Fire — Evacuation
overview: Building on fire. Priority is to get everyone out safely.

steps.title: Get out immediately
steps.description: Do not try to fight the fire or collect belongings. Get yourself and everyone else out immediately.

steps.title: Stay low under smoke
steps.description: Smoke rises — crawl low on the ground where the air is cleaner. Cover your mouth and nose with a damp cloth if available.

steps.title: Do not use lifts
steps.description: Use the stairs only. Lifts may fail or take you to the fire floor. Feel doors before opening — if a door is hot, do not open it.

steps.title: Close doors behind you
steps.description: As you leave, close (do not lock) doors behind you. This slows the spread of fire and smoke significantly.

steps.title: Call 112 once outside
steps.description: Once you are safely outside, call 112 immediately. Give the exact address and which floors are affected. Never go back inside for any reason.

title: Stroke
overview: Sudden brain attack caused by blocked or burst blood vessel. Use the FAST test.

steps.title: FAST test
steps.description: F — Face drooping on one side (ask them to smile). A — Arm weakness (ask them to raise both arms — does one drift down?). S — Speech slurred or confused (ask them to repeat a simple sentence). T — Time to call 112 immediately if any of these are present.

steps.title: Call 112 now
steps.description: Stroke treatment must happen within hours. Do not wait to see if symptoms improve. Every minute without treatment, brain cells die.

steps.title: Keep them comfortable
steps.description: Lay the person down with their head and shoulders slightly raised. Do not give food, water, or any medication — they may not be able to swallow safely.

steps.title: Note the time
steps.description: Write down the exact time symptoms started. Doctors need this to decide on treatment. Stay with the person and keep them calm until help arrives.

title: Seizure
overview: Uncontrolled electrical activity in the brain causing involuntary movements.

steps.title: Do not restrain
steps.description: Never hold the person down or try to stop their movements. You will cause injury. Let the seizure run its course.

steps.title: Clear the area
steps.description: Remove sharp, hard, or hot objects from around them. Place something soft under their head. Loosen tight clothing around the neck.

steps.title: Do not put anything in their mouth
steps.description: People cannot swallow their tongue during a seizure. Putting fingers or objects in their mouth risks injury to you and them.

steps.title: Time the seizure
steps.description: Note when the seizure started. Call 112 if it lasts more than 5 minutes, or if another seizure follows without the person regaining consciousness.

steps.title: Recovery position
steps.description: When the seizure stops, gently roll the person onto their side (recovery position) so saliva or vomit can drain. Stay with them — they will be confused and exhausted. Speak calmly.

title: Poisoning
overview: Person who has swallowed, inhaled, or been exposed to a toxic substance.

steps.title: Do not induce vomiting
steps.description: Unless specifically instructed by a medical professional or poison centre, do not make the person vomit. With some substances (acids, caustics, petrol), vomiting causes more damage.

steps.title: Identify the substance
steps.description: If safe to do so, identify what was taken. Keep the container, packet, or any vomit to show medical staff. Note when it was taken and how much.

steps.title: Call 112
steps.description: Call immediately. Tell them: what was taken, how much, when, and the person's age and weight. Follow their instructions exactly.

steps.title: Monitor and support
steps.description: Keep the person awake and monitor their breathing. If unconscious but breathing, place them in the recovery position. If they stop breathing, begin CPR.

title: Snake Bite
overview: Bite from a snake that may be venomous. Treat all snake bites as potentially serious.

steps.title: Keep the person still
steps.description: Movement increases the spread of venom through the lymphatic system. Sit or lay the person down immediately and keep them as calm and still as possible.

steps.title: Immobilise the bitten limb
steps.description: Keep the bitten arm or leg below heart level. Immobilise it with a splint or sling if available. Do not elevate it.

steps.title: Remove constricting items
steps.description: Remove rings, watches, and tight clothing near the bite before swelling begins. Do not remove clothing if it means moving the limb excessively.

steps.title: Do NOT cut, suck, or apply tourniquet
steps.description: Never cut the wound, attempt to suck out venom, apply a tourniquet, apply ice, or give alcohol. These all make outcomes worse.

steps.title: Get to hospital immediately
steps.description: Call 112 or transport the person to the nearest hospital. Note the snake's appearance if you can do so safely — but do not try to catch or kill it.

title: Road Accident
overview: Vehicle collision with injured persons. Make the scene safe before helping.

steps.title: Make the scene safe
steps.description: Turn on your hazard lights and park safely. If safe, turn off the crashed vehicle's engine. Do not smoke or allow anyone to smoke — fuel may have spilled.

steps.title: Call 112
steps.description: Call immediately. Give the exact location, road name, landmarks, and number of injured people. Stay on the line.

steps.title: Do not move injured people
steps.description: Unless they are in immediate danger (fire, rising water), do not move anyone who has been in a crash. Moving someone with a spinal injury can cause permanent paralysis.

steps.title: Control bleeding
steps.description: If someone is bleeding heavily, apply firm direct pressure with a clean cloth. Keep them warm with a blanket or jacket.

steps.title: Monitor consciousness
steps.description: Speak to the injured person calmly. Ask their name, where they are, what happened — this monitors their level of consciousness. Note any changes and report to ambulance crew on arrival.
